title: Alfresco's extension points are all node verbs, so a decision can only be inferred
content:
The registered policy interfaces are `BeforeCreateNodePolicy`, `OnCreateNodePolicy`, `OnMoveNodePolicy`, `OnUpdatePropertiesPolicy`, `OnAddAspectPolicy`, `BeforeDeleteNodePolicy` and their siblings. Every one is keyed to a document verb.

There is no `OnDecisionPolicy` and no `OnApprovalPolicy` — no business-event vocabulary anywhere in the extension surface. An integration that wants to capture "this application was accepted" has to infer it from an aspect being added or a property changing, which is the impedance mismatch stated in the platform's own API.

The vocabulary of a tool's extension points is a reliable predictor of what it can record. Where the hooks are node verbs, the records will be node events, however the feature is marketed.
description: Every NodeServicePolicies hook is create, move, update, delete or aspect-change. There is no OnDecisionPolicy, so an approval must be detected from an aspect being added.
